transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Rita Gomez (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Redwood CSM), Mark Reynolds (Pegasus CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Pegasus Head of Platform), Daniel Kim (Pegasus SRE)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Follow-up from the Sep 9th incident where Pegasus saw increased 5xx rate and elevated latencies during peak job dispatch. Discuss root causes, mitigations applied, changes to KV cache configuration and routing policy, request for more logs and a technical deep dive to validate fixes.

00:00 Liam: hey everyone thanks for joining, happy friday, uh we're gonna run through the incident follow-up from the 9th, try to be concise, Rita's got the timeline and then we'll go action items
00:14 Mark: thanks liam, appreciate it, want to make sure we cover what happened to our SLA, customers are asking for a summary and next steps
00:28 Rita: yep, quick recap — at 15:02 UTC on Sep 9th we saw a cascade where the dedicated pool started evicting a bunch of KV cache entries because of an autoscaler flapping event, that increased cold starts for a subset of model shards, which in turn pushed up latency and some internal timeouts, a subset of requests retried and hit the fallback route which was a smaller hosted endpoint causing capacity pressure there
01:02 Daniel: right and to add, we also had config drift on our side — some of the traffic shaping rules were rolled back during a deploy which increased fanout to Redwood by about 2.4x during that minute window, so it was multi-factor
01:25 Rita: yeah, so root causes we have so far: autoscaler threshold too sensitive, cache eviction policy misaligned with traffic patterns, and a routing policy that didn't fail over gracefully to a variant with better cold-start behavior
01:46 Sofia: can you explain the cache eviction bit — it sounds like keys were getting dropped too aggressively?
:02:01 Rita: essentially yes, the runtime's prefix/KV cache was tuned for average seq lengths and we had a spike of long sequences from a batch, the memory estimator tripped and evicted many prefixes; the eviction log shows TTL-based heuristics being applied, transcription maybe shows some names wrong, but logs attached.
02:30 Mark: were any customer data exposures a concern during this? we need to confirm no PII leaked
02:38 Anika: we ran the post-incident checks — no cross-tenant KV reads, KMS logs show no access anomalies; we will include the KMS audit dump in the postmortem doc
03:00 Liam: okay good — security concerns low, operational impact high. Rita, can you run through the mitigation steps you folks already applied?
03:15 Rita: Sure. Immediate mitigations on Sep 9: bumped autoscaler cooldowns and thresholds, disabled the aggressive byte-based eviction fallback, enabled a conservative hot-prefix pinning for top 5% of request prefixes, and temporarily diverted a small percentage of traffic to a dedicated warm pool. We also added an emergency route that reduces max seq length to avoid long-seq spikes hitting cache patterns.
03:47 Daniel: after those changes we saw 5xx drop from 4.8% to 0.6% within 12 minutes, but had some residual latency variance through the next hour
04:00 Sofia: what's the plan to prevent config drift on our side — I mentioned the deploy rollback, we need a guardrail
04:09 Liam: good point — Redwood recommends using the config lock feature on Dedicated for critical traffic-shaping settings; Rita will share a step-by-step and we can add a webhook that refuses deploys when critical flags are changed
04:35 Mark: timeline for this guardrail?
04:40 Rita: I can draft the playbook today; plan to have a config-lock runbook and a deploy gate in place by next week, target 2026-09-22 for gating live on staging and 2026-09-29 for prod if all goes well
05:02 Daniel: logs — we asked for more granular traces, current retention isn't long enough for our audit team, can Redwood extend trace retention for the dedicated pool?
05:16 Rita: yes we can increase retention as an add-on or temporarily export to your S3; we'll include retention increase options and costs in the follow-up doc
05:30 Liam: also we promised a replay — we'll run a controlled replay of the peak traffic on Dedicated staging to make sure the KV cache pins behave and autoscaler doesn't flare; that will be during the deep-dive
05:50 Sofia: about durable fallbacks — we don't want to hit hosted fallback, it's unacceptable for us, is there an option to pre-warm a second pool?
06:05 Rita: there is — pre-warmed hot pools are part of Redwood Dedicated commitments; we can propose a hotfix reservation for peak hours and set up warm pools in the same region to reduce cross-region fallbacks
06:24 Mark: cost implications? quick number please
06:30 Liam: rough ballpark: pre-warm pool for your peak footprint is roughly a 15-25% increase on committed GPU capacity; I'll put exact numbers and a short TCO in the doc
06:48 Daniel: on the technical root cause — you mentioned kernel selection and memory estimate logic, can we get into that?
07:00 Rita: briefly — the runtime chooses execution kernels and memory lanes based on sampled sequence distribution; the sampling window was too small so it didn't catch the long-seq spike, leading to suboptimal kernel choices and more memory pressure; also the quantization path has different memory footprint which exacerbated eviction
07:28 Daniel: can we change sampling window on the Dedicated cluster?
07:35 Rita: yes, we can adjust the estimator and increase sampling window for your cluster; that's a config change and we recommend doing it after we validate with the replay so we don't over-provision memory for normal traffic
07:52 Mark: customers want a formal postmortem doc — include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and what we will do to prevent recurrence, plus cost impact; we'll also need an executive summary for ops and a technical annex for SREs
08:12 Anika: we have a template we've used previously; I'll populate exec summary and list of stakeholders, and Rita will add the technical annex
08:28 Liam: action items check: Rita will extract logs and timeline, Daniel to provide extra traces, Liam to send pricing for hot-pool commitment, Anika to send the postmortem template; any others?
08:45 Sofia: include the SOC2/ISO audit notes — customers asking for that as well
08:52 Anika: yes, we'll attach our latest SOC2 report and KMS audit snippets
09:05 Mark: how does rollback detection work — is Redwood able to flag config anomalies during deploys?
09:13 Rita: there's a deploy anomaly detector we can enable; it watches config changes for critical flags and can block or flag them based on a policy; we'll propose a policy matching your workflow in the doc
09:34 Daniel: for the deep-dive, I want to bring two SREs and maybe the infra lead who owns the autoscaler; is that okay?
09:42 Liam: absolutely, the deep-dive will be SE-led; we'll do a 90-minute session and run the replay live; target tentative window Sept 21-23, we'll coordinate via calendar
10:00 Sofia: about the KV cache eviction heuristics, are there plans to have better observability — metrics per-prefix, eviction reasons?
10:12 Rita: yes, roadmap includes per-prefix eviction counters and eviction_reason metrics; for now we can surface detailed eviction logs to your S3 for the replay window
10:30 Mark: also want SLA credit conversation — our legal team will want clarity on credits if recurrence happens
10:38 Liam: we'll handle SLA credit conversation through the renewals channel, but we can outline the incident impact and proposed credits in the postmortem doc; we'll flag for our contracts team
10:55 Daniel: minor thing — some transcribed names in the raw logs are being autocorrected, might show Redwood product names wrong (e.g., KV cache spelled as K-V cash in a few lines) — just FYI when you ingest the transcript
11:12 Rita: noted, thanks. We'll also include a cleaned timeline and raw timeline for audit.
11:30 Anika: ok next steps recap: postmortem doc by 2026-09-17 with timeline, logs extract and recommended config changes; deep-dive week of 2026-09-20 with replay on staging; pricing/commit proposal by 2026-09-18
11:55 Mark: thanks everyone, appreciate the fast response, we'll review the doc and get Daniel's traces to you by end of day Monday
12:05 Liam: great, thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links — I'll drop the SOC2 and the playbook links in the notes
